title: Applied ML eval-harness: prompt sets, model onboarding, quantization profiles, and regression triage playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standards and operational procedures for the applied-ML evaluation lifecycle: eval harness usage, prompt-set design and benchmarking, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails, quantization profile validation, and regression triage. The document is intended for ML engineers, SREs, and applied researchers participating in model onboarding, rollout, and post-deployment regression detection.

Goals
- Provide a single, reproducible process for onboarding models into the eval harness and production serving.
- Standardize prompt sets and benchmarks to enable consistent quality comparisons across models and quantization variants.
- Define quantization validation profiles and expected signal coverage.
- Specify a regression triage flow with ownership, thresholds, and escalation paths.

Scope and audience
- Scope: open-models and proprietary model variants that will be served by Redwood (hosted, dedicated, private). Includes 1) eval-harness integration, 2) prompt set curation, 3) quantization profile validation, and 4) regression triage + rollback guidance.
- Audience: ML Engineers, Applied ML, Release Engineers, and Product Managers.

Key definitions
- Eval harness: Redwood's automated evaluation framework used to run batch prompt sets, compute metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/BERTScore/F1/accuracy/custom), and record outputs for regression monitoring.
- Prompt set: A curated set of inputs representing production workload slices (e.g., short-chat, system-instruction-following, code-completion).
- Quantization profile: A named configuration describing quantization settings (e.g., 8-bit, 4-bit, per-channel, GPTQ, intentional fused-kernel flags).
- Regression: A measurable drop in quality or a change in distribution of failure modes compared to a baseline (typically the previously deployed model/config).

Owner and contact
- Owners: Applied ML Team (applied-ml@redwood.example.com)
- Playbook maintainer: Maya Chen (author)
- Oncall for regression triage: Applied-ML rotation listed in the team roster

High-level process (summary)
1. Prompt set selection and labeling (owner: applied-ml)
2. Eval harness run with baseline and candidate (owner: eval-harness infra)
3. Quantization profile test runs (owner: quantization and runtime teams)
4. Automated quality checks and guardrails evaluation (owner: applied-ml)
5. Regression triage if checks fail (owner: oncall)
6. Rollout decision & canary (owner: release-engineering + product)

Detailed playbook sections

1) Prompt sets and benchmarks
Introduction
- Prompt sets are the canonical representation of production workload slices. Each set must include: name, description, dataset size, stratification attributes (e.g., length, domain, system vs user prompts), and labeling rubric.

Minimum metadata for each prompt set (table format)
| field | example | required |
|------|---------|---------|
| name | short-chat-1000 | yes |
| description | 1k short user utterances from chat product | yes |
| size | 1000 | yes |
| label_schema | {answerable:boolean, toxicity:int(0-4), correctness:int(0-5)} | yes |
| domain_tags | chat, faq | recommended |

Prompt creation guidelines
- Use production-sampled traffic where possible (anonymize and remove PII).
- When synthetic data is needed, mark as synthetic in metadata.
- Ensure balanced coverage: 10-20% edge cases, 60-80% common cases, 10-20% adversarial examples.
- Each example should have at least one human label for correctness and 20% should have double-annotated labels for inter-rater agreement checks.

Benchmarking procedure
1. Pick baseline model (currently: model-v3.1) and candidate model/quantization profile.
2. Run eval harness with consistent runtime and seed. Include deterministic tokenization steps.
3. Compute primary metrics (defined per prompt set) and store outputs in the eval-harness artifacts bucket.
4. Produce a summary CSV with per-example deltas and aggregate metrics.

CLI example
- Run baseline: ./eval-harness run --prompt-set short-chat-1000 --model model-v3.1 --out artifacts/baseline-short-chat-1000.json
- Run candidate: ./eval-harness run --prompt-set short-chat-1000 --model model-v4.0-q4_0 --out artifacts/candidate-short-chat-1000.json

2) Model onboarding checklist
Pre-onboarding (owner: model-owner)
- Verify licensing and model card information is in the Model Registry.
- Ensure model artifacts conform to storage and checksum policies.
- Provide expected latency/throughput targets and intended use-cases.

Onboarding steps (numbered)
1. Add model to eval-harness registry (eval-harness/configs/<model>.yaml) with metadata (architecture, tokenizer, vocab, expected sequence lengths).
2. Run smoke tests (100 prompts across key slices) to confirm functional correctness. Expected pass: 0 crashes, <0.1% invalid tokens.
3. Execute full prompt-set benchmark runs (see section 1) across the curated prompt-set suite.
4. Run quantization profiles (see section 3) against the model and store artifacts.
5. Generate a PRD-style onboarding report: latency, cost estimate per 1M tokens, metric deltas vs baseline, known failure modes.
6. Schedule cross-team review: runtime, SRE, product, security.

Acceptance criteria for production promotion
- No critical regressions on primary prompt sets (see guardrails thresholds).
- Latency p95 <= 1.25x baseline p95 for target sequence lengths, or documented fallback.
- Estimated cost per token within acceptable band agreed with product.
- Signed off by Applied ML owner and runtime lead.

3) Quality guardrails (automated checks in CI and runtime monitoring)
Guardrail categories and thresholds (examples)
- Correctness: primary metric delta <= -2% absolute or relative (configurable per prompt set).
- Toxicity: any increase in high-severity toxicity (>3 on rubric) > 1% absolute => fail.
- Safety / hallucination indicator: detected hallucinations > 2% absolute increase => warn/triage.
- Latency: p95 latency regressions > 25% => fail.

Automated gate in CI
- When a candidate is proposed, the eval-harness CI job runs the gateway prompt sets and evaluates guardrails. Jobs must pass full gate before allowing deployment to canary.

Human review triggers
- Any guardrail marked as FAIL triggers a mandatory human review meeting with applied-ml, runtime, and product.
- WARN triggers a lightweight triage by applied-ml owner.

4) Quantization profiles and validation
Supported profiles (examples)
- q8_per_channel: 8-bit per-channel symmetric quantization (fast, low-risk)
- q4_gptq: 4-bit GPTQ with per-tensor scale (higher risk, high compression)
- int8_static: int8 with calibration table

Validation tests
- Numeric regression: run a subset of deterministic prompts and compute token-level divergence (KL divergence on logits, top-1 match rate). Thresholds: top-1 match >= 95% for q8_per_channel, >= 90% for q4_gptq.
- Downstream metric regression: for each prompt set compute primary metric delta vs float baseline. Thresholds are stricter for high-sensitivity prompt sets (e.g., code-completion).
- Performance regression: measure p95 and throughput under continuous batching load. Quantized variants should meet configured latency SLO.

Example quantization test command
./quant-test --model artifacts/model-v4.0 --profile q4_gptq --prompt-set code-complete-500 --out artifacts/q4gptq-code-complete.json

Quantization profile metadata table
| profile_name | bits | technique | recommended_use_cases |
|--------------|------|-----------|----------------------|
| q8_per_channel | 8 | per-channel symmetric | general-purpose, low-risk |
| q4_gptq | 4 | GPTQ | cost-sensitive, controlled workloads |

Storage and traceability
- Attach quantization profile name and artifact checksums to model registry entry. All quantization outputs stored with eval-harness run id.

5) Regression triage playbook
Triggers for triage
- Automated guardrail fail during pre-release CI.
- Continuous monitoring alert: sustained quality drift (7-day rolling window) greater than configured threshold.

Initial triage steps (within 2 business hours)
1. Acknowledge alert in the incident channel and assign triage owner (applied-ml oncall).
2. Pull the failing run artifacts: baseline & candidate outputs, per-example diff CSV, and guardrail metric logs.
3. Run quick stratification: identify top 3 slices with highest delta (e.g., prompt length >512, code prompts, non-English).
4. If regression is isolated to a slice, attempt targeted mitigations (prompt routing, rollback of quantization profile, tweak decoding parameters).

Escalation criteria and steps
- If regression impacts primary prompt sets or >20% of traffic-equivalent slices: escalate to release-engineering + product for potential rollback.
- If root cause is infra (e.g., tokenization bug, serving mismatch), notify runtime and SRE with logs and revert to last-known-good binary.

Post-triage deliverables (within 72 hours)
- Triage report (title, date, owner, impact summary, artifacts, root cause hypothesis, mitigation, action items).
- If rollback occurred: annotated rollback timeline and communication plan.
- If a fix is produced: regression test case added to guarded prompt set and the eval-harness test suite.

6) Monitoring and alerting integration
- Key dashboards: per-model-for-deployed-version metrics (primary metric, toxicity, latency p50/p95), per-prompt-set deltas, and per-quantization-profile performance.
- Alerts: guardrail-fail (CI and runtime), sustained-drift (7d rolling window), latency-exceed(p95 threshold).

Example alert thresholds (prod)
- guardrail_fail_count > 0 (immediate, PagerDuty to applied-ml oncall)
- sustained_drift_percentage >= 3% for 7 days (SLACK alert + SRE)

Related artifacts and locations
- Eval harness repo: git@repo.redwood:eval-harness.git
- Prompt set catalog: s3://redwood-eval/prompt-sets/catalog.csv
- Model registry: https://model-registry.internal.redwood/models
- Artifacts: s3://redwood-eval/artifacts/<run-id>/

Appendix A: Example onboarding report template (fields)
- Model name, version, checksum
- Intended use cases and excluded uses
- Prompt sets evaluated with summary table (prompt_set, size, primary_metric_baseline, primary_metric_candidate, delta)
- Latency and cost estimates (p50/p95, cost per 1M tokens)
- Quantization profiles tested and numeric divergence summary
- Known failure modes and recommended mitigations

Appendix B: Quick checklists
- Pre-Canary checklist: guardrail CI pass, smoke tests pass, signed-off playbook entry, monitoring dashboards created, rollback runbook ready.
- Pre-Production checklist: canary monitoring stable for 24-72 hours depending on traffic, no sustained drift, incident budget within tolerance.

Revision history and maintenance
- Maintainer: Applied ML Team. Review cadence: quarterly or after any major incident.
- Last reviewed: 2026-06-15 (updated thresholds and q4_gptq guidance).

Contact and escalation
- Applied ML Slack channel: #applied-ml
- Oncall schedule: https://oncall.redwood.internal/applied-ml
- Security and privacy issues: immediately notify security@redwood.example.com

End of document.
